posts.text: Nick Saban, testifying in front of a Senate committee now, comes out strongly in favor of the Cruz-Cantwell college sports bill. Says the bill is needed because college sports are a mess headed for a much bigger mess.

Early numbers look great for Steve Hilton and Spencer Pratt both advancing to the California governor’s and LA mayor’s runoff. But since California counts votes like it’s still 1850 in the state, we will have to wait weeks for the final vote tallies to be complete. Ridiculous.

I get that half the country would rather the country get blown up in nuclear war than give Trump credit for anything. But just look at the numbers today compared to in June of 2022 and tell me how everything isn’t demonstrably much better across all metrics.

What benchmark would you like to use? Murder and life span seem significant. We are less likely to get murdered and more likely to live long lives than at any point in US history. Stock market is at an all time high & has nearly quadrupled since 2016 when Trump entered office.


Adam Matthew (@JNennski)

Clay - 2022 is not a benchmark we should be using.  Things suck right now. Things also sucked in 2022 and in 1979 and in 2008.   Stop pretending it’s great because less people are getting sh

This doesn’t even factor in the Covid shots or the fact that people were getting fired for not getting the shot — STILL — in 2022. Or still having to wear masks. This is just basic objective data. It’s light years better today than four years ago by all measures.

If I had predicted stock market would double, murders would fall by 50%, inflation would fall by 2/3rds & gas would be cheaper by 71 cents a gallon by June of 2026, y’all would have called me crazy. Things aren’t just better than Biden’s June of 2022, they are light years better

In June of 2022, gas prices averaged over $5 a gallon, inflation was 9.1%, the murder rate was 6.3 per 100k & S&P 500 was 3675. Four years later gas is cheaper,  inflation is roughly 3%, the murder rate is 4.0 per 100k, & the S&P 500 is 7600, more than double four years ago.

Scott Pelley has been fired by 60 Minutes. Pelley will soon find out that no one else in media will come close to paying him millions a year to do a few stories a year. I think a lot of these old school TV guys are delusional about their market worth in today’s media.

The data doesn’t lie. Are there other reasons than woke politics? Sure. The game is basically a three point shooting contest now, flopping, load management, tanking, there are many factors at play. But by the NBA Finals the teams are playing hard. I think it’s mostly politics.

Here’s the NBA Finals viewership graph. It fell off a cliff when LeBron, Silver and Kerr went woke and political and has never recovered. Jordan is the peak in 1998. Game 6 of the 1998 NBA Finals is still the most watched basketball game in American history. By far.

The Super Bowl and NCAA Tournament, meanwhile, are setting all time record highs. The NBA is posting somewhere around 1/3rd or 1/2 of the viewers it had back in 1998. Despite there being 50 million more people in the country today than in 1998.

Sure. NBC is counting broadcast TV and streaming numbers together, a metric that has never existed before. The NBA Finals will probably average around 14 million viewers this year, less than half of what Michael Jordan’s Bulls got in 1998, when way fewer people lived in the US.

“Don’t tell me that I shouldn’t feel the way that I feel!” People on social media, all day every day. But isn’t one of the biggest tests of adulthood not validating your every emotion as being rooted in legitimate fact, especially when it isn’t supported by facts at all?

It’s also the case that at a certain level money matters, but lottery winners who become fabulously wealthy, for instance, tend to revert to their overall happiness or unhappiness level before they won the lottery. Lots of people use money as a proxy for happiness. It often isn’t. Tons of insanely rich people are miserable.

Yet consumer opinion data is worse now than at any point in our last 50 years. Either things are truly the worst they have been in 50 years — that clearly isn’t true — or people feel like they are the worst they have been in 50 years. It’s the latter. So why? Social media is my answer. It’s feel, not reality.
